subject: Clarifying what Redwood retains by default — visibility and edge scenarios
messages:
From: Olivia Cheng <olivia@nexthealth.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick question on Redwood default retention for demo data

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — Dan and I had a quick follow-up for procurement/security. For our pilot we'll be sending sample chat traffic and some uploaded documents. Can you confirm what Redwood retains by default for: (1) raw user requests (the text/attachments we send), (2) model responses (the generated completions), and (3) intermediate streaming fragments / KV cache items?

A couple of extra asks: will any of these be replicated to analytics telemetry stores? And is the default retention window the same in the hosted product vs. Dedicated?

Appreciate a short, plain-language answer we can hand to our security team.

Best,
Olivia Cheng
Security & Integrations
NextHealth

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Cheng <olivia@nexthealth.ai>, Dan Park <dan.park@nexthealth.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on Redwood default retention for demo data

Hi Olivia / Dan — thanks for the clear list of asks, and great meeting earlier. High-level answers below; I'll attach a short matrix for clarity.

- Raw requests (user inputs and attached files): by default, hosted accounts retain request payloads for 30 days for product/quality analysis. Attachments referenced in requests are tokenized metadata and small file stubs in the retention store — not full binaries (we reference them in object storage with access logs).

- Model responses (completions): the final generated outputs are retained for 30 days by default in hosted. Responses that are explicitly marked as ephemeral by a "no-store" flag are not persisted.

- Streaming fragments & KV cache: transient streaming fragments and KV cache entries are short-lived by default and are not materialized in the long-term store unless the session is finalized. Typical streaming buffer TTL is ~2 hours; KV cache is persisted only for the life of the pinned session or until TTL expiry.

- Analytics/telemetry: we do copy lightweight telemetry (latency, token counts, error codes) into our aggregated analytics store for product metrics; this telemetry does not include unhashed request text. Audit logs may contain pointers and hashed identifiers for traceability.

- Hosted vs Dedicated: Dedicated gives you control to extend/shorten retention (configurable in the Dedicated console) and options to disable forwarding to centralized analytics. Hosted default is 30 days; Dedicated defaults depend on the customer's contract but can be configured to match your policy.

I'll attach the matrix (retention-matrix-v2.pdf) and a short erasure-evidence example. Kimberly and Marissa, could you review the language for a one-page note Olivia can pass to their security team?

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

On Sep 21, 2027, at 10:05 AM, Sean Gallagher wrote:
> I'll attach the matrix and an erasure-evidence example. Could you review the language for a one-page note Olivia can pass to their security team?

Draft language tweaks (short + precise):
- "Default retention window for hosted accounts: 30 days for request payloads and generated outputs. Attachments are referenced; full binaries are stored only if uploaded into object storage and governed by the customer's storage config."
- "Streaming buffers (in-memory fragments) are purged within 2 hours by default and are not written to the long-term store unless the session is finalized."
- "KV cache lives for the session duration and is evicted after TTL unless persisted by the application."
- "Telemetry for platform health (latency, token counts) is aggregated and contains no plaintext user inputs; audit logs may contain references for incident investigation."

Questions for legal/compliance: do we want to explicitly state the 30-day number in outbound customer-facing security letters, or leave it as "default short-term retention (30 days)"? Some customers want exact numbers for contract language.

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-09-21T12:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on Redwood default retention for demo data

Thanks — adding concrete examples so their security team can see edge cases: 

1) Demo web chat (single-session): user sends prompt + doc. Default hosted behavior: request and response retained 30 days; streaming fragments not persisted; attachments referenced as stubs with object storage metadata. If customer marks session with "no-store", nothing is written to long-term stores.

2) API batch job (high-throughput): request logs and final outputs kept 30 days; we keep aggregated telemetry for throughput tuning indefinitely (no raw text).

3) Dedicated (on-prem / VPC): retention governed by customer config — defaults in our installer are 30 days, but the customer admin can set retention to any value or enable auto-delete on a shorter cadence.

4) Redaction / erasure: we can remove request text and outputs on demand; proof of deletion includes object storage purge entries and a signed erasure token. See attached example (example-erasure-evidence.txt).

If NextHealth needs a shorter default to match pilot policies, we can scope an exception on Dedicated or add an early opt-out for hosted pilots (requires a support ticket and acceptance of potential reduced troubleshooting data).

Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Privacy & Evals
Redwood Inference
